key_insight: In layered titanates, absorbed water self-organizes into 1D chains and hydrated surface layers that enable fast, anisotropic proton transport.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a crystal-orientation and hydration-controlled route to design solid proton conductors for energy devices such as fuel cells and protonic electronics.
method: Scanning electron microscopy to map hydration-dependent microstructures
Density Functional Theory simulations to resolve ordered water arrangements and hydrogen bonding
Infrared spectroscopy and conductivity measurements to correlate structure with proton transport
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ordered 1D water chains at low hydration, hydrated (001) surfaces at higher hydration, and room-temperature proton conductivity up to 3 mS/cm along one crystal direction.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on hydration level and crystal orientation, so maintaining the water network in a device may be challenging under operating conditions.
paper_title: One-dimensional self-organization of water molecules in proton conducting Andersson-Wadsley titanates
